description: A machine learning-based video super resolution and frame interpolation framework. Est. Hack the Valley II, 2018.

summary.one_liner: Video2X is a C/C++ framework for upscaling video and interpolating frames using machine-learning models (Anime4K, Real-ESRGAN, Real-CUGAN, RIFE) over Vulkan.
summary.what_it_does: Video2X runs video super-resolution (upscaling) and frame interpolation as two modes. It supports Anime4K v4 and custom MPV-compatible GLSL shaders, and Real-ESRGAN, Real-CUGAN, and RIFE (all models) via ncnn and Vulkan. The README says version 6.0.0 is a rewrite in C/C++ that runs on Windows and Linux and requires no extra disk space during processing beyond the final output. Windows users get a GUI and installer, and Linux users can get AUR packages, an AppImage, or a container image. The README also describes a Google Colab notebook for free GPU use with session limits.
use_cases: interpolate frames to raise video frame rate
batch upscale video on Windows with a GUI
run video upscaling in Docker or Podman
upscale videos for free on Google Colab
how_to_run: Windows: download the installer from the GitHub releases page
Arch Linux: install the video2x package from the AUR
Other Linux distros: download Video2X-x86_64.AppImage from the releases page
Container: run the Video2X image from the GitHub Container Registry with Docker or Podman
Build from source: see the PKGBUILD file and the documentation for dependencies and commands
notable: Upscaling and frame interpolation in one tool, using several models (Anime4K v4, Real-ESRGAN, Real-CUGAN, RIFE)
Needs no extra disk space during processing beyond the final output, per the README
Packaged for Windows installer, Arch AUR, AppImage, and container images
GUI available in six languages on Windows
caveats: Precompiled binaries require AVX2 CPUs and a Vulkan-capable GPU
Platforms are listed as Windows and Linux; macOS is mentioned only for container images
Google Colab sessions are capped at 12 hours, and the README warns against back-to-back sessions
keywords: make low resolution video higher quality
